summary: Tested Morris V2 Global Search backend (/api/search) and frontend CommandPalette. 22/22 backend pytest tests pass after fixing one critical sort-key TypeError in /app/backend/global_search.py. Frontend palette verified: opens on Ctrl+K, all 14 scope chips present with correct data-testids, close button works, Esc closes, ArrowDown/Enter navigate, scope switching triggers re-fetch, results grouped by kind, mobile viewport works.
action_items: None — testing agent already fixed the one critical bug found (sort TypeError). Please confirm the fix in /app/backend/global_search.py (lines ~352-357) is acceptable.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: global_search.py `results.sort(key=_key, reverse=False)` blew up with TypeError comparing datetime to str when mixing collections (some rows store `updatedAt`/`createdAt` as datetime, some as isoformat str). Every `scope=all` request with results from mixed collections (including the default UX path used by the palette) returned 500. Coerced updatedAt to string before sorting.
Minor: /api/search does not enforce/validate `limit` upper-bound — a malicious caller could pass limit=10000. Consider clamping to <=100.

Minor: `_search_clients` aggregates by clientName|company lower-cased pipe key — two clients with same name at different companies with empty company field could collide. Not a bug today but worth noting.
Minor: `scope=drafts` filter is included but the list of SCOPES in the frontend does not expose a 'Drafts' chip. Backend supports it, UI doesn't. Either add the chip or document the omission.
Minor: Frontend debounce is 220ms — spec asks for 300ms. Not a bug, just an off-spec value.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for verified interactions (palette open/close, scopes, keyboard, mobile)

rca_of_the_issue: RCA: `results.sort(key=lambda r: r.get('updatedAt') or '', reverse=True)` in global_search.py failed with TypeError('<' not supported between instances of 'datetime.datetime' and 'str'). Some documents were auto-saved by /api/generate at server.py line ~949 using raw `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (datetime object), while newer collections store isoformat strings. Mixing produced a mixed-type sort key. Fix: coerce updatedAt to str before sort. Reproduction: GET /api/search?q=&scope=all as admin user with any auto-saved documents → 500. After fix → 200 with results.
